subtitles.text: As government services become more autonomous,
AI agents can access records, delegate tasks and carry out transactions.
But every action must stay within verified authority.
Meet Mariam, a fictional citizen. She asks to renew her residency permit.
Several AI agents work together on her application,
and WAKALA checks every protected action before it runs.
Now, in a separate test case, we deliberately trigger a security scenario.
The Insurance Agent requests another citizen's record.
Its identity is genuine, but this action exceeds its authority.
WAKALA blocks the request before any protected data is returned.
Blocking the request is only the beginning.
An authorized security officer signs in, reviews the incident,
and reassigns the legitimate work to a replacement agent.
The other agents keep their authority.
After the required officer approval, the application continues.
Mariam's renewal completes, and another citizen's application is unaffected.
In twelve hundred controlled synthetic tests, WAKALA allowed none of the seven hundred and twenty unauthorized operations,
and wrongly denied none of the legitimate ones.
Repeated recovery tests also completed under the tested conditions.
WAKALA is not another government AI assistant.
It is the security layer that makes autonomous government services accountable.
WAKALA. Autonomous AI. Accountable actions.
